reasoningSteps: Assume a synthetic twenty-turn planar coil with area 0.040 square metres, fixed surface normal and magnetic field increasing from 0.10 to 0.40 tesla in 0.20 seconds.
The flux linked to one turn is B times area times cosine of the angle between field and area normal; here the angle is zero and flux increases from 0.004 to 0.016 weber.
Compute the mean induced emf magnitude as 20 times (0.016 minus 0.004) divided by 0.20, obtaining 1.20 volts; a single-turn calculation would give only 0.060 volt.
With positive flux increasing, the signed emf is negative for the chosen positive loop orientation; the current direction, if the circuit is closed, opposes the increase.
If the field stays at 0.40 tesla rather than continuing to change, d-flux/d-time is zero and an ideal stationary loop has no induction despite substantial field strength.

Use Faraday's law with its explicit flux integral and derivative; a time-averaged ramp result is not proof of an instantaneous waveform. Primary reading: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-2/pages/13-1-faradays-law

vocabulary.definition: A magnetic field exerts a force q v × B on a charge moving with velocity v.

vocabulary.term: Electric Field
vocabulary.definition: The electric field at a point is defined as the electric force per unit positive test charge in the limit that the test charge does not disturb the source distribution.

vocabulary.term: Magnetic Force on Moving Charge
vocabulary.definition: The magnetic force on a charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B is q(v×B).

vocabulary.term: Magnetic Force on a Charge
vocabulary.definition: The magnetic force on a charge moving in a magnetic field is q times the cross product of velocity and magnetic field.
